svg.title: Quantized Inertia: proposed mechanism (schematic)
svg.desc: Two-panel schematic of McCulloch's proposed QI mechanism. Top: an object accelerating to the right sees a Rindler horizon at distance c^2/|a| behind it; fewer Unruh-wave modes fit between object and Rindler horizon than between object and the distant cosmic horizon, so radiation pressure is larger from the front and the net force opposes the acceleration (McCulloch 2013). Bottom: at very low acceleration the Unruh waves become comparable to the Hubble scale, waves that do not fit 2 Theta / n are disallowed on all sides, so inertial mass falls as m_i = m(1 - 2c^2/(|a| Theta)). Not to scale.
svg.text: Quantized Inertia: the proposed mechanism (schematic, not to scale)
A. Ordinary (high) acceleration: asymmetric Casimir effect between two horizons (McCulloch 2013)
region that can never signal the object
long and short Unruh waves fit (Hubble-scale cut only)
larger radiation pressure from the front
net force opposes acceleration → interpreted as inertia
B. Very low acceleration: Hubble-scale Casimir effect on Unruh waves (McCulloch 2007)
(the Rindler horizon, c²/|a| away, now lies beyond the cosmic horizon)
disallowed: Unruh waves that do not fit (λ ≠ 2Θ/n)
Unruh peak wavelength ≈ 4π²βc²/|a| grows as |a| falls
fewer allowed modes → less Unruh energy → less inertia:
mᵢ = m (1 − 2c² / (|a|Θ)), with a floor near |a| ≈ 2c²/Θ
Proposed by McCulloch; Unruh radiation has not been directly observed and the derivation is disputed (e.g. Renda 2019). Wave sizes are illustrative.
